text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-A Palestinian man hijacked a Bulgarian charter airliner on Tuesday and demanded to be flown to Norway. The hijacker surrendered quickly at Oslo's Gardermoen airport after asking for a lawyer and political asylum.

-Energy Minister Jens Stoltenberg says high electricity prices are not a result of free market pricing, but are due to high consumption. Norway is facing a potential power crisis later this year due to a lack of snow and rainfall last winter, which has left extremely low water levels at reservoirs for hydropower production.
-An analysis of 2,091 small and medium-sized Norwegian companies shows an increase in total turnover but a decrease in profitability. One in five of the companies showed a deficit in 1995.

-American group CMI International has entered negotiations with Norwegian authorities to build a new factory for car parts in Moss, near the Swedish border. CMI has already invested over 400 million crowns in a factory for aluminium car parts at Lista in southwest Norway.

-Norwegian banks disagree on how interest rates will develop over the next 12 months. Norway's larget commercial bank Den norske Bank said on Tuesday it expected a one percent rise during next year. Other major banks, however, believe rates will remain unchanged.
